name.text: Coordinates of the vertices of a cuboid

questiontext.text:

Its lowest corner P is \(({@x0@},\,{@y0@},\,{@z0@})\). generalfeedback.text:
Start at P and add the moves along each axis: the length changes x, the width changes y and the height changes z.

VertexMoves from P (x, y, z)Coordinates
V (above R)\({@L@},\ {@W@},\ {@H@}\)\(({@ta[1]@},\,{@ta[2]@},\,{@ta[3]@})\)
W (above S)\(0,\ {@W@},\ {@H@}\)\(({@tb[1]@},\,{@tb[2]@},\,{@tb[3]@})\)

Coordinates say how far along each of the three axes you must move from O; here we start from P and add the moves.

questiondescription.text:
Vectors II: coordinates of the vertices of a cuboid

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.6: Give the coordinates of vertices of a cuboid placed away from the origin, from one corner and the edge lengths.

Core

This question is adapted from Question A3 in Section A of Chapter 23 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Foundation 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: a cuboid away from the origin, with vertex lettering and the moves from SMP AS/A2 Core 4 for AQA Chapter 9 Question C2, new contexts and numbers, randomised, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Those are the edge lengths. V is that far from P, so add them to P's coordinates \(({@x0@},\,{@y0@},\,{@z0@})\).
You moved \({@W@}\) along x and \({@L@}\) along y. The length \({@L@}\) runs along the x-axis (P to Q).

falsefeedback.text: Your point is a move of \(({@mv[1]@},\,{@mv[2]@},\,{@mv[3]@})\) from P. V is above R: travel from P along the edges to R, then up to V. Each edge changes one coordinate by its length.

truefeedback.text: W is above S, and S is along the y-axis from P: the width \({@W@}\) changes y, not x.
Add the moves to P's coordinates; P is not at the origin.

falsefeedback.text: Your point is a move of \(({@mv[1]@},\,{@mv[2]@},\,{@mv[3]@})\) from P. W is above S: travel from P along one edge to S, then up to W. Each edge changes one coordinate by its length.
